Consider the following statements about the Vernacular Press Act, 1878:
(I) It empowered district magistrates to require printers/publishers to enter into a bond against publishing material causing disaffection.
(II) The magistrate's action under the Act was final, with no right of appeal in a court of law.
(III) It applied equally to both English and vernacular newspapers.
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: One of the Act's worst features was precisely its discrimination between English and vernacular press.

faqs.e: Wood's Despatch recommended English as the medium for higher studies and vernaculars at the school level — the reverse of statement II.
